name: MO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Wesley Bell running with $3.6M raised
Polymarket prices Bell at 98% to win
model.rationale: MO-1's +29 Democratic lean, Bell's incumbency and strong fundraising, and prediction markets pricing him near 98% all point to a comfortable hold; the Republican challenger has shown no financial or polling evidence of competitiveness.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major outside spending against Bell could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Wesley Bell, a first-term Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a St. Louis-area district that leans Democratic by roughly 29 points. He enters the general election with about $1.1 million on hand after raising $3.6 million, plus modest outside support, while Republican Paul Berry has reported no fundraising. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but Polymarket prices Bell's chances at about 98 percent.

The fundamentals strongly favor the incumbent: the district's partisan lean, incumbency advantage, and financial edge all point the same direction. The realistic question is the size of the margin, not the winner, with Bell positioned for a decisive victory in November.
